explanation: This edge is narrower than the one the atlas already carries from the coup. The dictatorship accepted Salazar’s terms because its own finances had failed, and that argument is made there. The March election added the authority to grant those terms. A government formed under a president confirmed a month earlier by a national vote made the appointment of April 1928, and the veto Salazar demanded bound every other ministry. A junta improvising its own legitimacy could not promise that. The claim here is about the terms and who could grant them. It says nothing about why he was wanted.
